trigger.observed: Root's actual boot7 completed the mandatory full RomFS hash for 3101 files, then stopped opening unimplemented pctl. No nnMain or frame was reached
trigger.measurement_boundary: Only missing pctl service acquisition was runtime-observed. Factory and Initialize request shapes below are independently statically measured SDK wrappers, pending a real post-adapter boot

independent_static_SDK_checks: PCTL Initialize at sdk+0x3fc050 calls PLT0x645c80 then sdk+0x3fcad0. Service-name table at SDK0xb5ea80 contains pctl,pctl:s,pctl:a,pctl:r

For each successful service acquisition the SDK converts the factory into a CMIF domain and calls factory virtual0x28 -> sdk+0x3fd334: command1 CreateServiceWithoutInitialize, sendPID plus raw u64 ClientProcessId placeholder0, no buffers or input handles, one output interface object

The SDK caches the first successful child and discards subsequently created successful children. It then calls cached-child virtual0x20 -> sdk+0x3fd4fc: service command1 Initialize, no raw IO, PID, buffers or handles
No restriction, permission, unrestricted-state, safety-level or parental-settings query is part of this measured initializer

implemented.factories: Four explicitly registered real service names pctl,pctl:s,pctl:a,pctl:r; service manager is unchanged, with no alias or forced-success fallback
implemented.CreateServiceWithoutInitialize1: CMIF4/6, required PID descriptor and raw u64 placeholder0, no buffers or input handles. Creates a distinct initially uninitialized child and returns a real MOVE interface session; generic ipc.c converts it to a domain object ID when requested through a domain
implemented.Initialize1: On a created child, no raw inputs/outputs, PID, buffers or handles. Sets only that child's local initialized lifecycle state under a mutex; repeated calls preserve that initialized state
implemented.family_identity: Factory family identity is preserved in every child, including service diagnostic names. No unverified family capability masks or privilege equivalence are invented. Every unmeasured policy/permission method fails for all four names
implemented.ownership: 32 child states are retained in a bounded process-lifetime pool; exhaustion explicitly fails. States are never freed or silently reused while generic cloned/copied IPC sessions could borrow them. This is a host allocation budget, not a claim about Horizon family session limits
implemented.guards: Checked host scratch at service open and commands; bounded raw argument sizes with unspecified CMIF alignment slack; required factory PID/zero placeholder; rejection of extra input handles, buffers and unsupported transport
implemented.pre_main: Constructor only registers names and function pointers; no environment, profile, settings, IPC object or guest access before main

policy_limits: Initialize establishes a local IPC object lifecycle only; it does not claim that parental restrictions are disabled, enabled, configured, checked or unrestricted
No host or guest parental-control settings, permission data, account state or system configuration are read or written
All restriction/permission/safety-level/settings/timer/event operations, legacy factory CreateService0 and unknown commands fail explicitly
The public primary sources confirm common factory interfaces but do not establish complete per-family capability masks; no general PCTL interface or privilege compatibility is claimed
General mutable-state reclamation across generic IPC clones/domains remains outside this narrow startup adapter; process-lifetime retention avoids a borrowed-state use-after-free

primary_references.used_for: Public client uses explicit service-family names, domain conversion, factory1 with PID/u64zero and one output object, then service1 with no IO. Libnx fallback order differs from this actual SDK's four-name iteration

Primary protocol research identifies all four names as IParentalControlServiceFactory and separates factory1 CreateServiceWithoutInitialize from child-service1 Initialize; policy/query methods are distinct commands
